targets.title: Cross-language priming asymmetries in lexical decision and episodic recognition.
targets.evidence_quote: Our first step is to establish the reliability of Jiang and Forster’s (2001) original results. To this end, we tested translation priming in a new sample of highly proficient Chinese–English bilinguals.
targets.outcome_quote: Experiment 1 succeeded in replicating the original finding by Jiang and Forster (2001)—namely, the existence of L2–L1 translation priming in an episodic recognition task— but failed to confirm the absence of priming in the L1–L2 condition in the same task.

targets.title: Lexical acquisition and the modular lexicon.
targets.evidence_quote: In this final experiment, a more powerful test of the episodic L2 hypothesis is carried out using a more robust form of priming, namely, repetition priming rather than translation priming. As explained earlier, it has been found that in an episodic recognition task, old words show strong masked repetition priming, but there is no priming for new words (Forster, 1985; Rajaram & Neely, 1992).
targets.outcome_quote: The findings are clear. In an episodic recognition task, Chinese– English bilinguals show repetition priming for both old and new English (L2) words. This contrasts sharply with the results for the monolingual English speakers, where repetition priming was ob- tained for old words only.
